personal.bio: Dual student of Business Informatics (B.Sc.) at FHDW Bielefeld with Deutsche Telekom AG as practice partner, specialising in Software Engineering. Day to day I design and build applications on the Pega Platform — currently rebuilding Telekom's idea-management system, before that migrating HR processes off a legacy system as a business analyst. Off the clock I run my own home server, live in Linux and open source, and use AI tools as part of my everyday development workflow.

caseStudy.name: LocalMeetingRecorder
caseStudy.intro: A desktop app that records meetings and turns them into transcripts and AI summaries — fully offline, because confidential conversations shouldn't travel to someone else's servers.

blocks.label: Problem
blocks.text: Cloud transcription tools are convenient, but every word of a confidential meeting ends up on external servers. In an enterprise context that is usually a hard no — so most meetings simply never get proper notes.

blocks.label: Approach
blocks.text: A Python desktop app built around faster-whisper: one-click screen and microphone recording through a minimal Tkinter GUI, FFmpeg for capture, and locally-run Whisper models for transcription plus bullet-point summaries. Model size is a deliberate user choice — from ~39 MB (fast) to ~1.5 GB (most accurate) — trading speed for quality on the user's own hardware.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.text: Recordings, transcripts and summaries are organized per meeting session and never leave the machine. No accounts, no API keys, no cloud — install, click record, get notes.
